settings.headline: Your binaries. Your servers. One control panel.
settings.subhead: Setu is a cPanel-style control panel for single-binary web apps. Rust, Go, anything that ships as one executable: give each app a domain, HTTPS, its own PostgreSQL database, nightly backups and updates that roll back. All on servers you own.

settings.heading: One command to install
settings.intro: On a fresh Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04 or Debian 12/13 server (x86_64 or aarch64), as root, with ports 80 and 443 open and a DNS name pointing at it. The installer brings PostgreSQL and Caddy itself.

settings.heading: From bare server to live app in three steps
settings.intro: Setu is a single binary. It is the control plane, the per-server agent and the small privileged helper, selected by subcommand.

items.label: Step 1
items.title: Install
items.body: Run the installer. It verifies the release against SHA256SUMS, sets up PostgreSQL and Caddy, starts the panel and prints a one-time setup URL.

items.label: Step 2
items.title: Add a server
items.body: The setup wizard registers this machine; add more with one `setu agent install` line. Agents only connect outward, and each server shows online within seconds.

items.label: Step 3
items.title: Add an app from a manifest
items.body: Paste or link a small TOML manifest, pick a domain, and Setu provisions the site: user, database, binary, systemd unit, HTTPS route, health check.

settings.heading: Everything a site needs, handled
settings.intro: No Dockerfiles to write, no runtime to maintain on the server. The app is a published binary and Setu runs it as a hardened systemd service.

items.title: Automatic HTTPS
items.body: Caddy sits in front, programmed through its admin socket, with one route per domain and certificates through ACME.

items.title: PostgreSQL for every app
items.body: Each site gets its own database and role, created for you and passed to the app through its environment.

items.title: Native systemd, real limits
items.body: Every site runs as its own user in a hardened unit, with memory and CPU limits enforced by cgroups. No container runtime in the path.

items.title: Nightly backups
items.body: Database and data directories are backed up on a schedule, and you can restore a site from the panel.

items.title: Updates that roll back
items.body: An update backs up first. If the new version does not come up healthy, Setu puts the old binary back and restores data when it has to.

items.title: Many servers, one panel
items.body: Agents long-poll the control plane over HTTPS, outbound only. Manage one box or a small fleet from the same place.

settings.heading: Built for single-binary apps
settings.intro: If it compiles to one executable, binds an address from the environment and answers a health check, Setu can run it.

items.title: Axum, Actix and friends
items.body: Publish a release tarball and describe it in a manifest. Setu does the rest.

items.title: Static Go services
items.body: One static binary, a port and a database URL from the environment is all it takes.

items.title: Anything compiled
items.body: Setu has no per-language knowledge. The manifest is the only app-specific thing it reads.

items.title: Miniflux and hello-axum
items.body: Sample manifests you can copy and adapt live in the manifests repository.

settings.heading: Why not Docker, Kubernetes or cPanel?
settings.intro: They are good tools for other jobs. Setu is for the case where you have a few compiled apps and your own servers.

items.title: Nothing to build or run
items.body: Containers still leave you to wire the proxy, certificates, database, backups and updates. Setu does that part, and the app stays a plain binary under systemd. Containers are on the roadmap if you need them.

items.title: No cluster to operate
items.body: A cluster is a lot of moving parts for a handful of binaries. Setu is one binary and a few systemd units that you can read and debug with journalctl.

items.title: Made for compiled apps
items.body: Hosting panels are built around PHP sites and shared hosting. Setu is built for Rust and Go services, and it is open source under AGPL-3.0.

settings.heading: Where it is going
settings.intro: Setu is early: expect rough edges before 1.0. Version 0.2 is planned to run anything and lose nothing. Plans can change.

items.title: Binary apps on your servers
items.body: Native systemd, Caddy HTTPS, per-app PostgreSQL, local backups with restore, updates with rollback, multi-server agents.

items.title: Containers (Podman)
items.body: Container images as a first-class runtime, rootless Podman under systemd.

items.title: Off-box encrypted backups
items.body: Nightly uploads to S3-compatible storage with retention and restore.

items.title: Cloudflare tunnel ingress
items.body: Serve sites from servers with no public IP.

items.title: Moves between servers
items.body: Move a site to another server, and drain a server without losing sites.

items.title: 2FA and alerts
items.body: Two-factor sign-in for operators, and email or webhook alerts when a site, server or backup fails.

settings.headline: Put your next binary on a server you own.
settings.subhead: Setu is free and open source. Read the docs, or go straight to the installer.
